problem:
A baseball is hit by a batter. The distance between the batter and the ball, measured in miles, is given by the function $s(t)$, where $t$ is the time in seconds. The values of $s(t)$ for different values of $t$ are given in the table below:

| $t$ | $0$ | $0.5$ | $1$ | $1.5$ | $2$ |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| $s(t)$ | $0$ | $0.015$ | $0.03$ | $0.045$ | $0.05$ |

Approximate the velocity ${s}^{′}(t)$ when $t=1$ using a backward difference approximation.

activity_context.topic_title: Estimating Derivatives Using a Backward Difference Quotient

feedback.problem:
The number of deer in a wildlife reserve, measured in hundreds, is given by the function $D(t)$, where $t$ is the time, in years, since the study began. The values of $D(t)$ for several values of $t$ are shown in the table below:

| $t$ | $0$ | $1$ | $2$ | $3$ | $4$ |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| $D(t)$ | $5$ | $7$ | $10$ | $14$ | $19$ |

Approximate the rate of change of the deer population when $t=4$ using a backward difference approximation. Do not round the answer.

The estimated rate of change when $t=4$ is
{{field-1}} hundreds per year.
feedback.worked_solution:
We use the backward difference approximation formula

$$
{D}^{′}(t)≈\frac{D(t)-D(t-h)}{h},
$$

at the time $t=4.$ We choose the step size $h$ to be as small as possible, in this case $h=1.$ This gives

$$
\begin{aligned}{D}^{′}(4) & ≈\frac{D(4)-D(4-1)}{1} \\  & =\frac{D(4)-D(3)}{1} \\  & =\frac{19-14}{1} \\  & =5.\end{aligned}
$$

So, the estimated rate of change when $t=4$ is $5$ hundreds per year.
